correctness.rationale: A generic one-parameter subgroup of the row-column torus has all matrix-coordinate weights distinct, so the ambient Grassmannian fixed points are exactly coordinate subspaces. For such a subspace, Chan--Ilten Proposition 2.3 identifies membership in either the determinantal or permanental Fano scheme with the same condition: the associated bipartite graph has matching number less than \(r\). Thus both projective varieties have the same finite fixed set, of cardinality \(B_{m,n,r}(k+1)\). Algebraic \(\mathbb C^*\)-localization gives the Euler formula. The extremal edge bound and the \(r=2\) star classification are elementary consequences of matching theory and were separately replayed by the packaged checker.

value.rationale: The determinant and permanent define parallel but geometrically different algebraic families, and their Fano schemes are central parameter spaces for linear spaces contained in those varieties. The theorem identifies a uniform global topological invariant shared by both families for every \(m,n,r,k\), and converts it exactly into the classical finite problem of counting fixed-size bipartite graphs with bounded matching number. The vanishing threshold is recovered immediately, while \(r=2\) yields a clean closed star formula. This is a family-level structural statement about the full Fano schemes, not a routine computation for one small component.
